subject: three shapes a real Scaleway account answered that no document declares (#431, #432, #436)
why: None of these could be found by reading anything. `dest_ip_range` is on the wire and in neither Scaleway's published document nor their own Go SDK; `default` is a literal path segment their SDK builds and this pack read as an identifier, so a declined operation answered 404 through a live route; `modification_date` is one of two dates a NIC carries and only one was served. The mutations put each back and require the test that names it to go red.

mutations.expect: a rule omits the key entirely, which is a shape the cloud never answers, on the create, the read, the update and both lists at once
mutations.label: a rule stops carrying dest_ip_range

mutations.expect: `default` falls back to matching {id}, finds no group and answers 404, which is how a declined operation stayed invisible to the client asking for it
mutations.label: the default segment is read as an identifier again

mutations.expect: the account-wide rules read as editable, so a client believes it can delete a filter it does not own and this emulator cannot remove
mutations.label: the default rules read as editable

mutations.expect: the default rules are minted afresh on every read, so a client that stored one finds a different rule set on the next call
mutations.label: the default rule identifiers move between reads

mutations.expect: a NIC answers a creation date and no modification date, on the create, the read and the list, which is what a real fr-par account contradicts on all three
mutations.label: a NIC loses its modification date
